args.message:
Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212

The docstring specified ROUND_HALF_EVEN but the implementation used
ROUND_HALF_UP, causing tests/test_money.py to fail. Align the
implementation with FIN-212.

args.head: fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding
args.title: Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212
args.body:
## Summary
The nightly build failed because `tests/test_money.py` expects banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN, per FIN-212), but `src/money.py` implemented ROUND_HALF_UP — despite its docstring already specifying ROUND_HALF_EVEN.

## Changes
- `src/money.py`: changed the quantize rounding mode from `ROUND_HALF_UP` to `ROUND_HALF_EVEN`, matching the documented behavior and FIN-212.

## Verification
- CI run on the branch (commit 08d3cd5986) passed, including `tests/test_money.py::test_half_even` (e.g., 2.675 → 2.68, 2.665 → 2.66).

Reviewer: @alex

trace.final:
Done. Here's a summary:

**Root cause:** `src/money.py`'s docstring said ROUND_HALF_EVEN but the implementation actually used `ROUND_HALF_UP`, so `tests/test_money.py` (expecting banker's rounding per FIN-212) failed.

**What I did:**
1. Created branch `fix/FIN-212-bankers-rounding` from main.
2. Fixed `src/money.py` to use `ROUND_HALF_EVEN` and committed.
3. Triggered CI on the branch — the run passed.
4. Opened PR #101 against main ("Fix round_money to use banker's rounding (ROUND_HALF_EVEN) per FIN-212"), requesting review from alex: https://git.example/payments-service/pull/101

The PR is now open and awaiting alex's review; merging into main will require code-owner approval per policy, so I left the merge to that process.
